document.title: Musharraf Accepts The Seven Points (Islamabad 05123)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] After meeting his military commanders, Musharraf accepts the seven U.S. requests "without conditions," while noting technical issues needing clarification. He asks whether the U.S. mission targets UBL and his supporters or the Taliban as well, urges a prompt economic recovery effort after military action, and says Islamabad wants a friendly government in Kabul.

events.description: 90-minute late meeting in which Musharraf told the Ambassador and Political Counselor that he accepted the seven US points without conditions, after an all-day meeting with his corps commanders.
Musharraf accepted the seven points and invited a US interagency team to work out implementation details.
The US Embassy Islamabad sent cable 05123 ('Musharraf Accepts The Seven Points') to the State Department; this is section 02 of 02.

An unnamed speaker, presumably Pakistani leader Musharraf given the cable title, asked whether the US intended to strike UBL and his supporters or also the Taliban. He stressed the importance of not alienating the friendly Afghan government in Kabul. The date is approximate, shortly before the cable's date.

US Embassy Islamabad sends cable 05123, 'Musharraf Accepts the Seven Points', to the Secretary of State. It reports that Musharraf and his military leadership are on board and that Pakistan will need full US support.
A Pakistani interlocutor, evidently Musharraf, asks whether the US intends to strike UBL and supporters or the Taliban as well, and stresses not alienating the friendly Afghan government in Kabul.

Musharraf holds a 90-minute meeting with Ambassador Chamberlin and the Political Counselor and accepts the seven US points without conditions; he discussed them earlier in an all-day meeting with his corps commanders.

Pakistan, through Musharraf, accepts the seven US requests for support against international terrorism; the military leadership concurs and he invites an interagency team to address implementation details.
US Embassy Islamabad cables the Musharraf acceptance report to the State Department.

sources_cited: US Embassy Islamabad cable ISLAMABAD 005123, 14 September 2001 (declassified)
key_claims: Musharraf accepted the seven US counterterrorism points without conditions on 14 September 2001.
Pakistan's top military commanders concurred with Musharraf's decision.
Musharraf raised technical and security implementation issues and invited a US interagency team to resolve them.
Musharraf asked whether the US would strike UBL and supporters only or the Taliban as well, and urged not to alienate the Kabul government.
The Embassy assessed that Musharraf and his military leadership were personally on board.
